tasks.name: Install floor protection at wood wall work zone
tasks.notes: Canvas drop cloth runners along base of wood wall work area. Wood wall is floor-to-ceiling — drips from brush/spray and sanding dust are the primary concern. Always required regardless of application method.

tasks.name: Mask ceiling at wall-ceiling junction
tasks.notes: Paper + tape masking at ceiling-wall junction to protect finished ceiling from overspray. Spray only — brush application typically needs no ceiling masking. 12-inch masking paper adequate for overspray drift. Key distinction from wainscot: wood wall meets ceiling directly (no cap rail), so ceiling_line zone replaces wall_adjacent zone.

sop_modules.name: Surface Preparation
sop_modules.notes: Prep tasks vary by substrate type and state. Caulk after fill/sand, before primer. MDF edge seal is mandatory for bare MDF — separate task before latex primer. Board-style walls (shiplap, T&G) have significantly more fastener holes and joint detail than panel-style walls.

tasks.name: Dust and clean all wood wall surfaces
tasks.notes: Remove construction dust, debris, and surface contamination from all wood wall surfaces. Tack cloth or damp wipe. First prep step. Board-style walls: clean groove channels thoroughly.

tasks.name: Sand wood wall per substrate and state
tasks.notes: Bare MDF: 220 grit faces. Bare FJP/softwood: 150-180 grit. Bare hardwood: 150-220 grit. Factory-primed (SS_PRIMED_FACTORY): scuff sand 150-180 grit for adhesion. All board/panel faces and any exposed frame members (library_panel).

tasks.name: Fill fastener holes and minor defects
tasks.notes: Fill nail/brad holes on boards or panel assemblies. QT3: fill obvious holes. QT4: fill all visible holes. QT5: fill every hole regardless of size, check with raking light. Board-style walls (shiplap, T&G) have significantly higher fastener density — each board nailed at every stud. Overfill-sand-flush method per Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine.

tasks.name: Sand filled areas smooth
tasks.notes: Sand all filled areas flush with 220 grit. QT5: check with raking light for uniformity. Rigid sanding block for flat panels (FFD §15.4.1). Flexible sanding sponge acceptable for shiplap/T&G grooves.

tasks.name: Caulk board-to-board or panel-to-frame joints
tasks.notes: Paintable acrylic latex caulk at internal joints. Board styles (shiplap, T&G): board-to-board V-groove or tight joints — note shiplap V-grooves may be left uncaulked by design to preserve board-line aesthetic. Panel styles (flat_panel, library_panel): panel-to-frame joints (horizontal and vertical). Joint density varies by wall_style — shiplap has highest density. Caulk quantity scales with wall SF.

tasks.name: Caulk wall-to-ceiling and wall-to-floor junctions
tasks.notes: Paintable acrylic latex caulk at wood wall perimeter: (1) wall-to-ceiling junction (or wall-to-crown when crown present), (2) wall-to-floor junction (or wall-to-baseboard when baseboard present). Continuous bead at top and bottom where wood wall meets adjacent surfaces. LF proportional to wall SF.

sop_modules.name: Primer Application
sop_modules.notes: CONDITIONAL — only runs when substrate_state = SS_BARE. Factory-primed (SS_PRIMED_FACTORY) substrates skip this module entirely. Primer type driven by substrate: MDF=SYS_PRIMER_MDF_LATEX (after edge seal), FJP=SYS_PRIMER_POPLAR_STAINBLOCK, hardwood=SYS_PRIMER_HARDWOOD_TANNINBLOCK, softwood=SYS_PRIMER_WOOD_ACRYLIC.

tasks.name: Prime wood wall surfaces
tasks.notes: Full primer coat on all wood wall surfaces. Spray: broad sweep passes on board faces or panel fields, detail on library_panel frame profiles. Brush: work systematically board by board or panel by panel. MDF: this is step 2 of two-step prime (edges already sealed). Thin coat in grooves (shiplap/T&G) and profiles (library_panel) — avoid buildup in recesses.

tasks.name: Light sand primer for finish coat adhesion
tasks.notes: 220 grit light sand entire primed surface. Provides tooth for finish coat. Flexible sanding sponge for shiplap/T&G grooves and library_panel profiles. Tack cloth after sanding.

sop_modules.name: Finish Coat Application
sop_modules.notes: Finish coat on all wood wall surfaces. Material system QT-driven: QT3=SYS_FF_STANDARD_ACRYLIC, QT4=SYS_FF_MODIFIED_URETHANE, QT5=SYS_FF_PREMIUM. Apply, tip once, walk away (FFD §15.3.1). Technique varies by wall_style.

tasks.name: Spray finish coat on wood wall
tasks.notes: Spray technique varies by wall_style: shiplap/T&G — sweep horizontal passes following board direction, maintain consistent distance to avoid pooling in grooves, light back-brush on grooves if needed. flat_panel — broad sweep passes, straightforward. library_panel — field panels first (broad passes), then HVLP or fine-finish tip for frame detail. Ceiling masking must be in place at wall-ceiling junction. Tall walls (H2+): back-check lower sections for drip accumulation.

tasks.name: Brush finish coat on wood wall
tasks.notes: Work board by board (shiplap/T&G) or panel by panel (flat_panel/library_panel). Apply, tip once, walk away (FFD §15.3.1). Flat panels: Roll and Tip methodology (FFD §15.6) for even coverage on large flat areas. library_panel: brush sized to profile, work panel-to-frame sequence. Tall walls (H2+): watch for runs collecting on lower boards/panels, back-check while upper sections are still wet.

sop_modules.name: Between-Coat Interstage
sop_modules.run_rule: Runs AFTER each coat EXCEPT the final coat
sop_modules.notes: Universal at ALL quality tiers. Sanding discipline varies by QT: QT3=spot sand only (nibs, rough spots), QT4=full 220 grit, QT5=thorough 220-320 grit. Rigid sanding block mandatory for defect removal (FFD §15.4.1). On large flat wood wall areas, rigid block sanding is particularly effective for leveling brush marks.

tasks.name: Clean work area between coats
tasks.notes: Remove dust, debris from floor protection and work area. Ensure clean environment for next coat.

tasks.name: Inspect previous coat
tasks.notes: QT3: quick glance at 6ft — obvious defects only. QT4: systematic scan at 3ft — all visible defects marked. QT5: lighted critical inspection at arm's length — zero tolerance. Key checkpoints: groove holidays (shiplap/T&G), panel-to-frame transition holidays (library_panel), drip accumulation on lower sections of tall walls.

tasks.name: Sand between coats
tasks.notes: QT3: spot sand nibs/rough spots only. QT4: full 220 grit entire surface. QT5: thorough 220-320 grit, uniform scratch pattern. Rigid sanding block mandatory on flat board/panel faces (FFD §15.4.1). Flexible sanding sponge acceptable for shiplap/T&G grooves and library_panel profiles.

tasks.name: Patch and repair marked defects
tasks.notes: Fill, sand, and spot-prime any defects found during inspection. Scope varies by QT.

tasks.name: Spot coat patched areas
tasks.notes: Touch-up patched areas to match surrounding finish before next full coat.

tasks.name: Tack cloth all wood wall surfaces
tasks.notes: Remove all sanding dust with tack cloth before next coat application. Cover every SF of wood wall surface. Work tack cloth into shiplap/T&G grooves and library_panel profiles.

tasks.name: Final quality inspection
tasks.notes: QT3: scan for obvious defects at 6ft. QT4: systematic review at 3ft of all surfaces. QT5: critical lighted inspection at arm's length. Key checkpoints: groove holidays (shiplap/T&G), panel-to-frame transition holidays (library_panel), brush marks on large flat areas, drip accumulation on lower sections (tall walls), caulk line quality at perimeter junctions, overall sheen uniformity.

tasks.name: Touch-up defects found during final inspection
tasks.notes: Correct any remaining defects. Feather touch-ups into surrounding finish. QT5: may require full additional coat if defects are widespread.

tasks.name: Remove ceiling masking
tasks.notes: Score tape edge before removal. Pull at 45-degree angle to prevent ceiling damage or paint peel. Ceiling_line zone teardown — distinct from wainscot wall_adjacent teardown.

tasks.name: Remove floor protection
tasks.notes: Remove canvas drop cloths from wood wall base perimeter. Fold inward to contain debris.

tasks.name: Vacuum work area
tasks.notes: Vacuum floor area after protection removal. Remove sanding dust and debris.

tasks.name: Clean tools and equipment
tasks.notes: Clean brushes, spray equipment, dispose of consumables. Water cleanup for waterborne products. Solvent cleanup for shellac-based MDF edge sealer residue.

workflow_sequence.standard_bare: MOD_WDWL_SETUP > MOD_WDWL_PREP > MOD_WDWL_PRIME > MOD_WDWL_INTERSTAGE > MOD_WDWL_FINISH_COAT(1) > MOD_WDWL_INTERSTAGE > MOD_WDWL_FINISH_COAT(2) > MOD_WDWL_FINAL_INSPECT > MOD_WDWL_CLEANUP
workflow_sequence.standard_factory_primed: MOD_WDWL_SETUP > MOD_WDWL_PREP > MOD_WDWL_FINISH_COAT(1) > MOD_WDWL_INTERSTAGE > MOD_WDWL_FINISH_COAT(2) > MOD_WDWL_FINAL_INSPECT > MOD_WDWL_CLEANUP
workflow_sequence.qt5_brush: MOD_WDWL_SETUP > MOD_WDWL_PREP > [MOD_WDWL_PRIME] > [MOD_WDWL_INTERSTAGE] > MOD_WDWL_FINISH_COAT(1) > MOD_WDWL_INTERSTAGE > MOD_WDWL_FINISH_COAT(2) > MOD_WDWL_INTERSTAGE > MOD_WDWL_FINISH_COAT(3) > MOD_WDWL_FINAL_INSPECT > MOD_WDWL_CLEANUP
workflow_sequence.notes: Prime module conditional on substrate_state = SS_BARE. QT5 brush adds additional FINISH_COAT + INTERSTAGE cycle per FFD §15.10.3. Single paintable item (ITM_WOOD_WALL_PANEL, SF) — no internal component sequencing needed. Height varies per room — estimation engine applies MOD_HT via PS_META.HEIGHT_BAND.
